title: Bayesian Retraction Optimization for Tissue Attachment Mapping in Surgical Dissection
summary: With growing surgeon shortages, automating surgical sub-tasks such as tissue dissection offers a promising step toward reducing workload and expanding patient access. Prior work has relied on hand-crafted incision policies that cannot quantify uncertainty or has relied on simulation-based methods that require strong modeling assumptions. We instead view tissue attachment identification as an inherently probabilistic problem and propose a Bayesian approach that avoids explicit tissue modeling. Our method uses a Sequential Bayesian Hilbert Map (SBHM) to represent the likelihood that each tissue point is attached to the underlying resection surface. An ensemble of learned classifiers predicts attachment likelihoods from spatial data acquired during robotic tissue retraction, with each classifier serving as a noisy information source to update the SBHM. To plan the next retraction, we devise Bayesian Retraction Optimization (BRO) to select the most informative action under safety constraints. As the SBHM refines over time, regions with high attachment likelihood are selectively incised. We validate our method in simulation across diverse tissue geometries and acquisition strategies, and demonstrate zero-shot transfer to real robotic dissection experiments.
tldr: Proposes a Bayesian approach (Sequential Bayesian Hilbert Map + Bayesian Retraction Optimization) for mapping tissue attachment in robotic surgical dissection, avoiding explicit tissue modeling and validated in simulation and real hardware.
tldr_zh: 提出一种贝叶斯方法（序贯贝叶斯希尔伯特图 + 贝叶斯回缩优化），用于机器人手术解剖中的组织附着映射，避免显式组织建模，并在仿真和实际硬件中得到验证。
summary_zh: 随着外科医生短缺问题的加剧，自动化手术子任务（如组织 dissection）为减少工作负担、扩大患者就医机会提供了有前景的途径。以往的研究依赖于无法量化不确定性的手工制定切口策略，或依赖于需要强建模假设的仿真方法。我们转而将组织附着识别视为一个本质上具有概率性的问题，并提出了一种避免显式组织建模的贝叶斯方法。我们的方法使用序列贝叶斯希尔伯特图（SBHM）来表示每个组织点附着于底层切除表面的可能性。一组经过学习的分类器从机器人组织回缩过程中获取的空间数据中预测附着可能性，每个分类器作为有噪声的信息源来更新SBHM。为了规划下一次回缩，我们设计了贝叶斯回缩优化（BRO），用于在安全约束下选择信息量最大的动作。随着SBHM随时间不断优化，附着可能性较高的区域被选择性地切除。我们在不同组织几何形状和采集策略的仿真中验证了该方法，并展示了其在真实机器人解剖实验中的零样本迁移效果。

title: MedDDC-Eval: Diagnosis-Decoupled Evaluation of Multi-Turn Medical Consultation Agents
summary: Multi-turn medical consultation agents must decide what to ask, adapt to patient responses, and determine when the collected evidence is sufficient. However, coupled evaluation conflates the quality of the policy-elicited history with policy-specific terminal diagnosis generation: strong generation can compensate for a thin history, while weaker generation can obscure a rich one. We introduce MedDDC-Eval, a diagnosis-decoupled testbed that treats elicited history as the comparison object and holds the history-to-diagnosis mapping constant through a shared frozen reader. Across two held-out sources, a grounded interface and an auditable diagnosis-trajectory-efficiency (D/T/E) harness measure diagnostic usefulness, information acquisition, and efficiency. Directional semantic coverage followed by deterministic one-to-one assignment yields coherent precision-recall counts for open-ended items, with at most one credited match per prediction or reference. Holding histories fixed, changing only the diagnostic reader shifts diagnosis F1 by 2.2-19.0 points and reverses 18% and 36% of pairwise policy orderings on the Record and Dialogue splits. We further apply standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) over interactive multi-turn rollouts to post-train Qwen3-32B using diagnosis-result and trajectory feedback. On the 100-case Record and 70-case Dialogue splits, the trained policy improves over its initialization by 9.7 and 4.6 total-score points; removing either primary signal lowers held-out joint performance. These results show that MedDDC-Eval supports controlled attribution, interpretable elicited-history measurement, and evaluation-guided evidence-acquisition policy development.
tldr: This paper introduces MedDDC-Eval, a diagnosis-decoupled evaluation testbed for multi-turn medical consultation agents that treats the elicited history as the comparison object and uses a shared frozen reader to isolate history quality from diagnosis generation. It also applies GRPO to post-train a policy using trajectory feedback, demonstrating improved performance.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了MedDDC-Eval，一种诊断解耦的多轮医疗咨询代理评估平台，将生成的对话历史作为比较对象，并通过共享的冻结阅读器将历史质量与诊断生成分离。还应用GRPO利用轨迹反馈对策略进行后训练，展示了性能提升。
summary_zh: 摘要：多轮医疗咨询代理必须决定询问什么、适应患者回应，并判断何时收集到的证据已足够。然而，耦合评估将策略引导的病史质量与特定策略的终端诊断生成混为一谈：强大的生成能力可弥补薄弱的病史，而较弱的生成能力则可能掩盖丰富的病史。我们提出MedDDC-Eval，一种诊断解耦的测试平台，它将引导获取的病史作为比较对象，并通过共享的冻结阅读器保持病史到诊断的映射恒定。在两个保留来源上，一个基于基础的接口和一个可审计的诊断轨迹效率（D/T/E）工具，分别衡量诊断有用性、信息获取和效率。定向语义覆盖后接确定性一对一分配，为开放式项目生成连贯的精确率-召回率计数，每个预测或参照最多有一个认可的匹配。固定病史不变，仅更换诊断阅读器即可使诊断F1分数变化2.2-19.0点，并在Record和Dialogue数据划分上分别逆转18%和36%的成对策略排序。我们进一步在交互式多轮推演中应用标准组相对策略优化（GRPO），利用诊断结果和轨迹反馈对Qwen3-32B进行后训练。在100例的Record划分和70例的Dialogue划分上，训练后的策略相比其初始值分别提升了9.7和4.6总分数点；移除任一主要信号都会降低保留集上的联合性能。这些结果表明，MedDDC-Eval支持可控归因、可解释的引导病史测量以及评估引导的证据获取策略开发。

title: Deep learning-based prediction of time-resolved adhesive forces in viscoelastic Hertzian contacts
summary: Fast prediction of the response of adhesive soft viscoelastic contacts represents a current challenge in soft robotics and for gripping and manipulation tasks. Determining the complete time-resolved force trajectory requires full numerical simulations, whose computational cost is strongly parameter-dependent, making them impractical for real-time application or design-optimization loops. In this work, we overcome this limitation by training a scalar-conditioned, stateful, sequence-to-sequence deep learning model to predict the full force evolution from a prescribed displacement history for both short- and long-range adhesion regimes. The data set spans four orders of magnitude in loading and unloading rates and includes varied dwell times, with the Tabor parameter ranging from $0.2$ to $3.2$. To enable learning across these heterogeneous time scales, we introduce a fixed-measurement-step (FMS) representation that converts variable-length trajectories into fixed-length sequences while preserving their physical-time information. Different architectures were trained, including long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, temporal convolutional neural (TCN) networks, and time-distributed dense layers with three different Tabor-conditioning mechanisms. The models were compared using global waveform and error metrics. We found that the best-performing model has an LSTM architecture with concatenated conditioning, which achieves a held-out mean-squared error of $5.0\times10^{-4}$, a median pull-off-force error of $\approx2.2\%$, and a median hysteresis error of $\approx1.1\%$. For the held-out protocols, the model predicts a complete force trajectory with a median inference time of $0.16$ s. The model is tested across unseen parameter combinations and against analytical limiting cases, providing a rapid surrogate for repeated numerical evaluations with potential use in control-oriented applications.
tldr: This paper introduces a deep learning model (LSTM with concatenated conditioning) that predicts time-resolved adhesive forces in viscoelastic Hertzian contacts as a fast surrogate for full numerical simulations, achieving low error and fast inference, with potential applications in soft robotics gripping and manipulation.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种深度学习模型（采用拼接条件的长短期记忆网络），用于预测粘弹性赫兹接触中随时间变化的粘附力，作为完整数值模拟的快速替代方案，实现了低误差和快速推理，在软体机器人抓取与操作中具有潜在应用。
summary_zh: 摘要：快速预测粘附性软粘弹性接触的响应是当前软体机器人以及抓取与操控任务中的一项挑战。要确定完整的时变力轨迹需要全数值模拟，但其计算成本强烈依赖于参数，使得此类模拟在实时应用或设计优化循环中不切实际。在本工作中，我们通过训练一个标量条件化的、有状态的序列到序列深度学习模型来克服这一限制，该模型能够从给定的位移历程预测完整的力演化过程，适用于短程和长程粘附机制。数据集覆盖加载和卸载速率四个数量级，并包含不同的停留时间，塔博尔参数范围从$0.2$到$3.2$。为了能够跨这些异质时间尺度进行学习，我们引入了一种固定测量步长（FMS）表示方法，将变长轨迹转换为固定长度序列，同时保留其物理时间信息。我们训练了多种架构，包括长短期记忆（LSTM）网络、时序卷积神经网络（TCN）以及采用三种不同塔博尔条件化机制的时间分布密集层。使用全局波形和误差指标对模型进行了比较。我们发现性能最佳的模型为采用级联条件化的LSTM架构，其在留出集上的均方误差为$5.0\times10^{-4}$，中位拉脱力误差约为$2.2\%$，中位滞后误差约为$1.1\%$。对于留出协议，模型预测完整力轨迹的中位推理时间为$0.16$秒。该模型在未见过的参数组合以及解析极限情况下进行了测试，为重复数值评估提供了一种快速替代方案，并有望用于面向控制的应用中。

title: Biological Amnesia in ICU Time-Series Prediction: A Drift-Adaptive Two-Stream Architecture with Temporal Retrieval
summary: Background: Clinical decision support systems degrade silently as treatment protocols evolve, yet standard adaptation methods treat models as monolithic blocks, unable to distinguish stable patient physiology from shifting institutional practice. Methods: We propose an adaptive clinical intelligence architecture for ICU intervention prediction that structurally decouples physiological from treatment representations, confining parameter updates to the treatment stream upon a dual distributional and accuracy trigger. Automated audit logs record which treatment features drove each adaptation event and how their importance shifted. At inference, an attribution-driven Temporal RAG module grounds each prediction in patient-specific, era-matched PubMed evidence anchored to the patient's dominant physiological features. Experiments used 84,792 MIMIC-IV stays (2008-2022) under strict chronological split. Results: Drift localised entirely to the treatment stream, validating the structural prior. Selective adaptation improved vasopressor and septic shock discrimination and calibration over the static source model. A fully retrained baseline yielded marginally higher aggregate discrimination but missed 26 septic shock cases the framework correctly identified, with none in the reverse direction; retrieval consistency with the pre-adaptation source model was preserved by the framework but degraded substantially in the retrained baseline. Conclusions: Structurally constraining adaptation to drifting components while preserving stable physiological representations enables clinical AI to evolve with practice without distorting learned patient biology. This architecture offers a template for governable, interpretable deployment of adaptive models in high-stakes clinical environments.
tldr: A drift-adaptive two-stream architecture for ICU prediction that decouples stable physiological representations from shifting treatment patterns, using a Temporal RAG module to ground predictions in era-matched evidence.
tldr_zh: 一种针对ICU预测的漂移自适应双流架构，将稳定的生理表征与变化的治疗模式解耦，并利用时间检索增强生成模块将预测锚定到匹配时代的证据中。
summary_zh:
**摘要：**  
**背景：** 临床决策支持系统会随着治疗方案演变而悄然退化，然而标准的自适应方法将模型视为单一整体，无法区分稳定的患者生理状态与变化的机构实践。  
**方法：** 我们提出了一种用于ICU干预预测的自适应临床智能架构，该架构在结构上解耦了生理表征与治疗表征，基于双重分布与准确性触发机制将参数更新限制于治疗流。自动化审计日志记录了每次自适应事件所驱动的治疗特征及其重要性的变化。在推理阶段，一个基于归因驱动的时间RAG模块将每个预测锚定到患者特有的、匹配时代背景的PubMed证据上，并关联患者的主要生理特征。实验使用了严格按时间顺序划分的84,792例MIMIC-IV住院记录（2008-2022年）。  
**结果：** 漂移完全局限于治疗流，验证了结构性先验的有效性。选择性自适应在血管加压药与感染性休克判别及校准方面优于静态源模型。完全重新训练的基线模型在整体判别上略有提升，但遗漏了框架正确识别的26例感染性休克病例，而反向遗漏为零；框架保持了与自适应前源模型的一致性，但重新训练的基线模型在该一致性上显著下降。  
**结论：** 在结构上将自适应约束于漂移成分，同时保留稳定的生理表征，可使临床人工智能在不扭曲已学习到的患者生物学特征的情况下随实践演进。该架构为高风险临床环境中可管控、可解释的自适应模型部署提供了模板。

title: Quality Action Assurance: Multimodal Verification of Examiner Claims in VR OSCEs
summary: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are the gold standard for assessing clinical competence, yet scoring remains vulnerable to examiner subjectivity, fatigue, and cognitive bias. Standard examiner validation via inter-rater statistics lacks explanatory power regarding the source of errors, as it neither analyzes examiner reasoning nor verifies examiner claims against actual events. Thus, we introduce Quality Action Assurance (QAA), a multimodal framework that verifies examiner claims in Virtual Reality (VR) pediatric OSCEs by comparing actions claimed by examiners against the true sequence of events, constructed from video, VR logs, and actor data. QAA combines a constrained temporal action alignment model, which performs action localization and actor source attribution, with a large language model that extracts examiner claims and checks them against the record. Across a 5-fold cross-validation, QAA achieves 99.2% $\pm$ 0.7% Actor F1 and 93.4% $\pm$ 1.9% W@16 for temporal alignment. Overall, QAA detects examiner errors with 70.0% precision and 76.7% recall, improving factual correctness from 39.2% to 79.2%, enabling fairer OSCE assessment.
tldr: This paper introduces Quality Action Assurance (QAA), a multimodal framework that verifies examiner claims in VR-based Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) by aligning claimed actions with ground-truth events from video, VR logs, and actor data, achieving high factual correctness improvement.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了质量行动保障（QAA）框架，通过将考官声明的动作与视频、VR日志和演员数据中的真实事件进行对齐，在VR客观结构化临床考试（OSCE）中验证考官声明的正确性，显著提高了事实正确性。
summary_zh: 摘要：客观结构化临床考试（OSCE）是评估临床能力的金标准，但其评分仍易受考官主观性、疲劳和认知偏差的影响。通过评分者间统计进行的标准考官验证缺乏对误差来源的解释力，既无法分析考官的推理过程，也无法对照实际事件核实考官的声称。因此，我们引入了质量行动保证（QAA），这是一种多模态框架，通过将考官声称的行动与基于视频、VR日志和演员数据构建的真实事件序列进行比对，在虚拟现实（VR）儿科OSCE中验证考官的声称。QAA结合了约束时间动作对齐模型（可执行动作定位和行动者来源归因）与大语言模型（可提取考官声称并与记录进行核对）。通过五折交叉验证，QAA在行动者F1分数上达到99.2% ± 0.7%，在时间对齐的W@16指标上达到93.4% ± 1.9%。总体而言，QAA检测考官错误的精确率为70.0%，召回率为76.7%，将事实正确性从39.2%提升至79.2%，从而实现了更公平的OSCE评估。

title: DobicVLM: Aligning Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Clinically-Grounded Programmatic Rewards via Group Relative Policy Optimization
summary: Medical imaging is a cornerstone of diagnostics, yet automated chest X-ray report generation struggles with structural adherence, anatomical completeness, and semantic faithfulness. We introduce DobicVLM, a vision-language model combining supervised fine-tuning on MedGemma-4B with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and clinically-grounded programmatic rewards. Our approach uses interpretable, rule-based reward components; structural verification, anatomical checklist, semantic similarity, and length constraints to enforce clinical standards without neural reward models. Trained on 1,000 de-identified image-report pairs from a private clinical dataset (with ethics approval and compliance to local regulations), DobicVLM is evaluated via blinded expert review on 69 held-out cases. DobicVLM outperforms Gemini 2.5 Flash across the majority of criteria, achieving the highest impression accuracy (27.2%) and medical terminology (86.5%) compared to both Gemini 2.5 Flash and MedGemma 4B baselines, with minor trade-offs in completeness and referrals. This demonstrates GRPO's value for transparent alignment in resource-limited settings. Keywords: Vision-Language Models, Radiology Report Generation, Reinforcement Learning, Medical AI, GRPO
tldr: DobicVLM combines supervised fine-tuning and group relative policy optimization with clinically-grounded programmatic rewards to improve chest X-ray report generation, outperforming baselines on impression accuracy and medical terminology in a small private dataset.
tldr_zh: DobicVLM结合监督微调和基于临床规则的程序化奖励的群体相对策略优化（GRPO）来改善胸部X光报告生成，在小型私有数据集上的印象准确率和医学术语方面优于基线模型。
summary_zh:
医学影像是诊断的基石，然而自动胸部X光报告生成在结构一致性、解剖完整性和语义忠实性方面仍面临挑战。我们提出DobicVLM，这是一种视觉-语言模型，结合了基于MedGemma-4B的监督微调、群体相对策略优化（GRPO）以及基于临床事实的程序化奖励。我们的方法使用可解释的、基于规则的奖励组件——结构验证、解剖清单、语义相似性和长度约束——在不依赖神经奖励模型的情况下强制执行临床标准。该模型在来自私有临床数据集的1000个去标识化图像-报告对（经伦理批准并符合当地法规）上进行训练，并通过盲法专家评审对69个保留病例进行评估。与Gemini 2.5 Flash相比，DobicVLM在多数标准上表现更优，在印象准确性（27.2%）和医学术语（86.5%）方面均取得最高分，优于Gemini 2.5 Flash和MedGemma 4B基线，仅在完整性和转诊建议上略有折衷。这证明了GRPO在资源受限环境下实现透明对齐的价值。  
关键词：视觉-语言模型，放射学报告生成，强化学习，医学人工智能，GRPO
